correctness.rationale: A root-path edge increases expected rooted PD iff all its descendant leaves otherwise become extinct; at common extinction q this contributes q raised to its clade size. The cumulative-profile inequality implies polynomial dominance by exact summation by parts. A canonical exhaustive recursive enumeration covers exactly 1,1,2,3,6,11,23 unordered rooted full binary shapes with 2 through 8 tips, finding a dominating tip for each through seven and all but one at eight. For the exceptional shape the only competitive polynomials differ by q^3(q^2+q-1), proving the unique open-interval change. A separate all-subset rational enumeration confirms the edge identity for every candidate tip of the exception at three exact rational q values. Exhaustive finite enumeration covers only n<=8; continuum correctness rests on exact inequalities.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior formula gives G_x(q) mechanically once a tree and a leaf are selected. It has no universal leaf-ordering assertion, sharp minimum n, or unique shape class. In the present restricted model, an explicit cumulative-dominance census is required for all n<=8; the exceptional golden-ratio polynomial then follows from its two competing ancestry profiles. The mathematical newness claimed is the sharp finite classification, not a new algorithm for a single value.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The model is a rooted unit-edge, equal-risk specialization of established HED/HEDGE expected-PD formulas. An equivalent statement would be a smallest rooted-binary shape in which the maximizer of the homogeneous HED polynomial changes with common extinction probability. The inspected texts supply the polynomial calculation, not the first-failure classification. Exact equality of the formulas is acknowledged, so no novelty is claimed for the underlying scoring method.

originality.rationale: The published general HED/HEDGE expected-PD formulas and general efficient algorithms are prior work and expressly excluded from the novelty claim. Inspected primary full texts do not state the sharp eight-taxon first-failure theorem, unique exceptional rooted unit-edge binary topology, or exact changeover constant. Actual database and literature queries for equivalent rank reversals and clade profiles found no stronger covering statement. The 2006 original full text was inaccessible, and equivalent unindexed or differently named finite classifications remain a bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: Hartmann and Steel 2006 original article was available only as abstract in this review; it is relevant to more general expected-PD optimization.
The 2016 I-HEDGE priority source full text was not accessible; public descriptions address iterative protection, not this sharp single-step homogeneous first-failure census.
An unindexed exact small-tree HED ranking table or an equivalent clade-size-ordering theorem could exist.

value.rationale: Choosing one species to protect under unknown common extinction risk is a natural conservation-priority question within the established HED/HEDGE framework. With risks and edge lengths equal, a switch would arise from topology alone. The theorem identifies the least taxon count permitting that phenomenon, classifies every shape at the first failure size, and specifies the unique shape and exact risk threshold. The result is not claimed for time-calibrated or heterogeneous real-world conservation networks and provides a structural baseline rather than empirical predictions.
